title: A systematic review of literature reviews on artificial intelligence in education (AIED): a roadmap to a future research agenda
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of understanding the rapidly expanding but fragmented literature on artificial intelligence in education (AIED). Rather than reviewing primary studies directly, the authors conduct a systematic review of literature reviews to synthesize what prior reviews have found, identify dominant themes, and map gaps in the field. Their goal is to provide an overarching roadmap for future AIED research and practice.

The study uses PRISMA-guided systematic searching across major education and technology databases and includes 143 journal-based literature reviews on AIED. The analysis is organized using a technology-enhanced learning framework, coding each review by publication year, country, venue, stakeholder group, educational level, subject area, review method, educational objectives, technologies used, and reported advantages/challenges. Although the paper is broad rather than intervention-specific, it includes discussion of AI uses such as machine learning, chatbots, intelligent tutoring systems, and large language models/generative AI in educational settings.

The reviewed literature spans multiple educational contexts, with the heaviest emphasis on higher education, followed by K-12, and a much smaller set focused on special education and early childhood. Across the review corpus, students and teachers are the primary stakeholders, while administrators and researchers receive much less attention. The paper concludes that AIED is most often positioned to support teaching and learning, assessment, and personalization, but that major concerns remain around privacy, equity, reliability, lack of teacher training, and the risk that AI may be seen as a replacement for human judgment rather than an augmenting tool. The authors call for more work on K-12, special education, and ethical, collaborative human–AI use.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / large language model chatbots used in education for content generation, instructional support, questioning, and feedback rather than a specific branded product.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a systematic review of reviews on AI in education. It synthesizes literature that includes teacher-facing and student-facing generative AI uses, especially chatbots and large language models, but does not evaluate one specific named product.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature reviews, generative AI and LLMs were discussed as increasingly important in education, with 19.5% of the reviewed studies focusing on LLMs/generative AI and 9.5% on chatbots. The paper notes that these tools are being used for teaching and learning support, including answering frequently asked questions and helping teachers plan and carry out lessons, but it does not report a pooled effect size.
findings.measure: Frequency of review coverage and described uses in the literature review corpus

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of literature reviews, so it synthesizes secondary evidence rather than reporting a primary causal estimate. The review is methodical and PRISMA-based, but the extract provides no quantitative effect estimate for a specific tool.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests broad relevance of generative AI in education, especially for teacher support and instructional tasks, but it does not quantify impact on learner outcomes. Without an effect size, the magnitude of impact remains unclear.
